metadata.description: Check whether two values are equal.
comments: equal(x, y) returns true if x and y are structurally equal under the type's notion of equality.
Requires an 'equality' type-class constraint on the argument type, which is the closest Hydra equivalent to Haskell's Eq instance.

Equality is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive (no NaN-style exception on floating-point: floating-point equality is provided per the underlying host's IEEE 754 comparison rules, so NaN /= NaN at the level of float64/float32).
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (==) :: Eq a => a -> a -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.equality.equal.structuralEquivalence
provisions.statement: equal returns true exactly when its two arguments are structurally equivalent under the type's equality notion -- identical scalars, or recursively equivalent collection contents regardless of construction/insertion order for sets and maps, and in the same order for lists.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.equality.equal.collectionContentsCompared
provisions.statement: equal compares collection (map/set) values structurally, not by a proxy such as a stringified representation -- two non-empty collections with different contents are never reported equal, including when a decimal value is nested inside a collection rather than appearing at the top level.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.equality.equal.decimalScaleSensitive
provisions.statement: equal treats two decimals of equal numeric value but different scale as unequal -- decimal equality is exact (value and scale), not numeric-value equality.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.equality.equal.ieee754ExtendedFloatSemantics
provisions.statement: equal on float64/float32 follows IEEE 754 extended totalOrder semantics rather than native host ==: NaN is equal to itself, and -0.0 is unequal to +0.0; ordinary finite values compare by numeric value.

metadata.description: Check whether two values are unequal.
comments: notEqual(x, y) = logic.not(equal(x, y)); this defining equation is the specification, and the default implementation.
Requires an 'equality' type-class constraint on the argument type.
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (/=) :: Eq a => a -> a -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.equality.notEqual.negatesEqual
provisions.statement: notEqual(x, y) = not(equal(x, y)) for scalar values of any type -- integers, strings, and floats.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.equality.notEqual.negatesEqualOnCollections
provisions.statement: notEqual on collection values (lists, sets, maps) is likewise the negation of equal: order-sensitivity for lists and order-independence for sets/maps carry through unchanged.
